tasks.title: Fleet rollout
tasks.notes: Step 1 (branch claude/connected-m6, PR #38, master de019ee): hub-side rollout orchestration — a rollout stages one sealed release across an ordered sequence of cohorts (canary first) of enrolled targets; RolloutService.advance drives each current-cohort target through the ordinary single-environment prepare/approve/execute path, opens the next cohort only when every target in the current one verified, and pauses on any target failure so later cohorts never start. Pause/resume/retry/withdraw, CLI (rollout-create|advance|pause|resume|retry|withdraw|rollouts) and admin REST routes, hub schema v10 (dbvc_ac_rollouts, dbvc_ac_rollout_targets), ConnectedRolloutTest (3 tests, 135 assertions). Step 2 (branch claude/connected-m6-page, 2026-09-21): the hub Rollouts admin page — the Rollouts React component (src/connected-app/index.js) with a cohort composer, a rollout list, and a detail view with Advance/Pause/Resume/Withdraw, per-cohort/per-target tone badges, Retry on a failed target, and expandable per-target rendering evidence (execution receipt outcome + warnings incl. generated_css_rebuilt); a Roll out shortcut on a sealed release. No new backend (wraps the step 1 routes). Verified by production build, wp-scripts lint-js, the connected-environments group, and a built-in-browser render of the built bundle in light and dark. No fleet-wide atomicity claim. Step 3 (branch claude/connected-m6-retention, 2026-09-21): retention — RolloutService.prune(days, dry_run) (default 30d) deletes terminal rollouts (completed/withdrawn/failed) older than the window with their target rows via RolloutStore.prune/prunable_count; running and paused rollouts and the approvals/preparations audit trail are untouched. wp dbvc agency rollout-prune [--days] [--dry-run], POST agency/rollout-prune, and a Prune finished dialog on the page (days input + dry-run preview). ConnectedRolloutTest now 4 tests / 164 assertions (retention test); connected-environments group 91 tests. Live-verified on the dbvc-codexchanges LocalWP site (master 94fade2) 2026-09-21: enabling the hub migrated the agency schema v8->v10 (both rollout tables created via dbDelta on the live DB), all 8 dbvc/v1/agency/rollout-* routes + the CLI (status/rollouts/rollout-prune/rollout-create) responded, and the hub Rollouts admin page rendered in real wp-admin (list + detail + cohort tables + tone badges + Advance/Pause/Withdraw + Prune dialog + evidence link) driven by a seeded fixture; the fixture was removed and the hub gate restored to its prior off state (schema stays v10, additive/harmless). M6 complete and live-verified.

tasks.title: Media / attachment transfer
tasks.notes: Step 1 (branch claude/connected-media-step1, PR #50, master 00638f6): the read-only foundation for attachment transfer — no bytes, no transport, no apply. New MediaReferences helper (addons/connected-environments/src/Preparation/MediaReferences.php) enumerates a wp.service body's attachment references (featured image _thumbnail_id, inline wp-image-<id>, wp-content/uploads/ URLs), resolves whether the target already holds each (authoritative _dbvc_original_attachment_id mapping for ids; attachment_url_to_postid / _dbvc_original_source_url for URLs), and builds the portable descriptor (sha256: content hash + mime/filename/relpath/filesize/url/title/alt/caption) the byte channel fills in step 2 — reusing the base plugin's DBVC_Media_Sync::format_hash + _dbvc_original_* conventions; creates nothing. DependencyLedger now reports each wp.media reference as present (target holds it -> no longer blocks) or unresolved (media_transfer_pending -> still blocks, so a post is never applied with a dangling id/URL), and detects the featured image (previously undetected -> would have applied a dangling _thumbnail_id). Fixes the latent gap that ANY released service post with an inline image or upload URL could never prepare READY (ledger blocked on both unresolved AND unsupported, and media was stamped unsupported). Tests: new ConnectedMediaTest (detection incl. featured image + dedup, mapping/URL resolution, descriptor hash, ledger present/unresolved transition); updated ConnectedReleaseTest ledger expectations (media unsupported -> unresolved). connected-environments group 99 tests / 2690 assertions. agent-docs refreshed (0 unmapped). PHPUnit-verified on real WP+MySQL; no cross-site run needed (read-only, no behaviour crosses the wire yet). Step 2 (branch claude/connected-media-step2, PR #52, master ffa9e1b): byte transport — media rides as a sibling channel to the body (never inside it; body stays hash-locked to after_hash and out of the seal digest). Source (ReleaseWorker::serve_payload_requests) attaches a wp.service item's referenced attachments as inline base64 via MediaReferences::collect_for_transport() (resolve_source resolves body ids/URLs to local attachments; deduped by content hash; per-file 2 MiB / per-item 4 MiB / count 25 caps from new Protocol::MAX_MEDIA_* constants; over-cap/unreadable -> deferred, never dropped; media-bearing payload posts on its own via chunk_payloads). Hub (accept_payloads -> sanitize_media) re-decodes/size-caps/re-hashes every entry against its declared hash (mismatch dropped), re-enforces caps, stores valid + deferred on the new dbvc_ac_release_items.media column (hub schema v10->v11, additive), reports media:{stored,deferred}. Target (pending_for_target) delivers media beside body; prepare receipt unchanged (bytes never echoed back). Tests: ConnectedMediaTest (source builder) + ConnectedReleaseTest round trip (valid+mismatch+oversize -> {stored:1,deferred:2}); connected-environments group 102 tests / 2735 assertions; PHPUnit-verified, no cross-site run (transport already live-proven, media validation is hub logic under test). Step 3a (branch claude/connected-media-step3, PR #54, master 48d7fa6): portable content-hash refs + convergence. Operator-approved design decision - a media-bearing wp.service post must converge under the hash contract (Comparison::environment compares source/target/baseline projection hashes; the hub baselines a verified apply to the source after_hash), so local attachment ids/URLs in the projection would make the target read perpetually 'incoming'. Fix: attachment refs become portable content-hash tokens (dbvc-media:<sha256>) in the projection. MediaReferences reworked to a token API - tokenize()/detokenize() (lossless, content-addressed; caches _dbvc_media_hash; unresolvable refs left literal), tokens_in_body(), local_by_hash(), hash-based collect_for_transport() (supersedes step-1 id-mapping). ServicePostObserver::snapshot() tokenizes before hashing (projection hash now site-independent - media-bearing posts re-hash once = one-time re-observe/re-baseline on the live site; media-free posts unchanged); apply_body() detokenizes before the guarded write; Applier::apply_service_item UNCHANGED (the after_hash verify now passes for a media post the target already holds; compensate/rollback detokenize the same way). DependencyLedger resolves tokens present (holds by hash -> converges, no block) / unresolved (blocks). ApprovalService::pending_for_target now delivers media on apply-requests too. Tests: ConnectedMediaTest (tokenize/detokenize round trip, ledger, transport, and a convergence proof - apply onto a target holding the same bytes re-projects to the source after_hash); connected-environments group 100 tests / 2720 assertions; PHPUnit-verified (no cross-site run - domain/projection logic under test). No hub schema change in 3a. Step 3b (branch claude/connected-media-step3b, PR #56, master 32d2e6a): sideload carried bytes - images now LAND on a target that lacked them, and the post converges. New MediaMaterializer: for each carried media entry, reuse a byte-identical local attachment (by content hash, no dupes) or sideload a new one from the base64 bytes (wp_upload_bits -> WP's own upload/type check gates the file, then wp_insert_attachment + wp_generate_attachment_metadata), stamping _dbvc_media_hash (+ base-plugin _dbvc_original_* identity, alt) so local_by_hash and the projection resolve it; bytes re-hashed against the declared hash before writing. Applier::apply_service_item materializes the item's carried media BEFORE apply_body detokenizes, journals created attachment ids (step:'media', created_ids -> step 4), and discards created attachments if the write is refused/fails verify (no orphans); reused attachments never touched. DependencyLedger: a carried token is present ('carried') so the post prepares READY even when the target lacks the bytes (neither-present-nor-carried still blocks); Preparer threads the prepare-request item's carried media hashes into build(). Tests: ConnectedMediaTest (materialize sideloads-then-reuses, rejects hash mismatch, ledger carried->present) + ConnectedApplyTest end-to-end proof (source attachment deleted, fresh target lacking it applies the release, bytes sideloaded into a new local attachment, post references it, converges to the source after_hash); connected-environments group 104 tests / 2776 assertions; PHPUnit-verified (real WP+MySQL). No hub schema change. M7 STEP 3 COMPLETE (3a portable projection + convergence, 3b sideload) - a media-bearing wp.service post transfers end to end and converges under the hash contract. Step 4 (branch claude/connected-media-step4, PR #58, master 9e4c539): reviewed rollback deletes only apply-created media - closes the media lifecycle. Applier::rollback reads the reversed operation's journal for its step:'media' created_ids (per container) and, after a wp.service before-image restore verifies, MediaMaterializer::discard()s exactly those ids (journalling a step:'media'/discarded entry); only attachments apply CREATED are deleted, a reused/pre-existing one is never touched, and nothing is deleted on a failed/restore_conflict rollback. Safe because a created attachment's content hash was absent before the apply, so the restored before image cannot reference it. Reviewed deletions need nothing (trashing a post neither creates nor removes attachments; rollback untrashes with media intact). Test: ConnectedApplyTest::test_reviewed_rollback_deletes_only_the_attachments_the_apply_created (after-state references one attachment the target holds = reused + one it lacks = sideloaded; after apply both present, after rollback the sideloaded one deleted, the reused one survives, post back at before image); connected-environments group 105 tests / 2821 assertions; PHPUnit-verified. No hub schema change. M7 COMPLETE for wp.service (transfer 1-2 + apply/converge 3 + clean rollback 4) - a media-bearing service post transfers end to end and converges under the hash contract. Deferred optional addendum (not blocking): media for Bricks content refs (a global class/variable could carry an upload URL; the token/materialize path lives in ServicePostObserver and would extend to the Bricks option-collection projection) + two capacity refinements (fetch-by-hash for files over the 2 MiB inline cap; offload stored bytes out of the DB column). Not yet cross-site live-verified (PHPUnit only). Plan recorded in docs/implementation/active/connected-environments-agency-control.md (## M7). LIVE-VERIFIED 2026-09-24 on the real installs (net-zero both sides): hub-side the v11 dbvc_ac_release_items.media column stored and returned the base64 payload out-of-body on dbvc-codexchanges's real hub DB (enabling the hub migrated schema v10->v11 with the media column; throwaway release removed, hub gate restored to off); connector-side the full media pipeline ran on the real dbvc-connectedsite-a WordPress with a real PNG - the observer tokenized the featured image to a content-hash token, collect_for_transport gathered the real bytes, a target lacking the media SIDELOADED a new real attachment (with real wp_generate_attachment_metadata), apply_body detokenized so the post referenced it, the post CONVERGED to the source after_hash, and rollback discarded the created attachment (net-zero, no _dbvc_media_hash residue). The cross-site HTTPS transport between hub and connector was already proven by M5 (same payload channel); a single continuous cross-site media round trip was not run (needs a 2nd disposable connector) but the pipeline is proven end to end on real WP split at the wire.
